say-how-many-steps.description: The W3C advises saying on the first step how many steps follow and on each step how far along the user is, for example "Step 2 of 4" [1].

w3c-multi-page-forms.title: W3C Web Accessibility Initiative, Forms Tutorial: Multi-page Forms

a-head-start-finishes-more.description: Car-wash loyalty cards with two pre-stamped stamps out of ten were redeemed by 34% of customers, against 19% for blank cards; the transfer from loyalty cards to a setup guide is an inference [1].

nunes-dreze-endowed-progress.title: Nunes and Drèze, The Endowed Progress Effect: How Artificial Advancement Increases Effort

minimal-still-needs-a-way-out.header: Minimal still needs a way out
minimal-still-needs-a-way-out.description: A minimal manual, centred on real tasks, taught faster than a standard manual in a study of 64 students, but beginners still need error-recovery material, which is why every step has a troubleshooting box [1][2].

lazonder-minimal-manual.title: Lazonder and van der Meij, The minimal manual: is less really more?

kalyuga-expertise-reversal.title: Kalyuga, Ayres, Chandler and Sweller, The Expertise Reversal Effect

four-pieces-one-chain.title: Four pieces, one chain
four-pieces-one-chain.script: Here is the whole route in four pieces: a terminal, an AI agent, a folder and a skill. Each piece only works because the one before it works, so when the last one runs, you know the whole chain holds. It takes about twenty minutes, and you can stop after any step and come back.

skip-what-you-have.title: Skip what you have
skip-what-you-have.script: If you already have an AI agent installed, jump straight to step five, because nothing before it changes for you. And if you would rather build the setup yourself than download it, the last Section is for you, so skip to the end.
